Package io.elepay.client.charge.webhook

Class Webhook

java.lang.Object
io.elepay.client.charge.webhook.Webhook
public final class Webhook extends Object
Verify signatures on webhooks sent by elepay.

elepay signs every outgoing webhook with an HMAC-SHA256 of <timestamp>.<raw-body> using the webhook endpoint's signing secret, and includes a header of the form: 

elepay-Signature: t=1713624000,sign=5257a8e9c4...

Typical usage in a servlet or Spring controller: 


 String payload = new String(request.getInputStream().readAllBytes(), UTF_8);
 String header  = request.getHeader(Webhook.HEADER_NAME);
 try {
     Webhook.verifyHeader(payload, header, signingSecret);
     // The payload is authentic — parse and dispatch.
 } catch (SignatureVerificationException e) {
     // Reject with HTTP 400.
 }

Read the raw body before any JSON parsing — the signature is computed over the exact bytes elepay sent, so any reformatting (whitespace, key order) will invalidate the match.

This class is stateless and thread-safe.

  • Method Details

    • verifyHeader

      public static void verifyHeader(String payload, String sigHeader, String secret) throws SignatureVerificationException
      Verify a webhook using the default 300L-second tolerance and the system clock.
      Parameters:
      payload - the exact raw request body as sent by elepay
      sigHeader - the value of the elepay-Signature header
      secret - the signing secret configured on the webhook endpoint
      Throws:
      SignatureVerificationException - if the header is malformed, the signature does not match, or the timestamp is outside the tolerance

    • verifyHeader

      public static void verifyHeader(String payload, String sigHeader, String secret, long toleranceSeconds) throws SignatureVerificationException
      Verify a webhook with a custom tolerance. Pass toleranceSeconds <= 0 to disable the timestamp check entirely (replay-attack prevention becomes the caller's responsibility).
      Throws:
      SignatureVerificationException
